benchmark: PE defect benchmark (stage K-1 of docs/kuhnian-path.md)

fields.origin: corpus (a defect this programme actually committed, with its source) | seeded (a constructed defect covering a property the corpus has not yet failed) | external (a defect from outside the author's corpus; K-1 targets >= 20)
fields.layer: record (the ledger misstates what happened) | design (the experiment could not grade the claim) | instrument (the checker or converter itself was wrong)
fields.detected_by: what actually found it: audit, derivation, computation, the linter, a reader
fields.enforced_by: the pe_lint property that refuses the recorded defect, or 'none' (a gap)
fields.fixture: defective + repaired ledgers the runner materializes; the expected finding must fire on the first and nothing may fire on the second

entries.title: Unrestricted admissibility absorbs every choice record
entries.defect: With a menu-dependent admissible set fit to the data, the observer model reproduces any finite choice record by admitting only the option chosen. No record can fail it.
entries.repair: Modular identification: identify components on evidence disjoint from the choices predicted; fix admissibility by an independent constraint (olgc.tex Prop. 5).

entries.title: Retained subspace of an isotropic moment
entries.defect: The rank-k budget kept the top eigenspace of a workload moment that was isotropic by construction (uniform options, ideal at the centroid; 833.33*I). Two calibration draws gave directions 56 degrees apart against 60 for random. The retained directions were sampling noise.
entries.detected_by: cold reread + computation of the population moment
entries.repair: Register an eigengap statistic with a threshold; build a workload with a gap (the D1 repair, s10.11).

entries.title: Treatment built the predicted response
entries.defect: Showing pre-projected values changed the stimulus, not the evaluator's resolution, and the class label came from the same fitted metric: the contrast reduces to (2p-1)^2 and could not have failed. A random-plane placebo reproduced it (0.9531, 0.9688 vs 0.9683).
entries.repair: Manipulate the evaluator, not the stimulus; require a placebo arm in the registration.

entries.title: Manipulation destroyed the instrument
entries.defect: Turning deliberation off left the evaluator 89-98% position-driven (2, 7, 1, 2 of 64 pairs graded). The manipulation removed the comparison, not its resolution.
entries.repair: Register an instrument-invariance bar (position-bias rate under treatment) as an instrument gate.

entries.title: Unparsed responses scored as disagreement
entries.defect: run_level scored answers cut off at max_tokens=1024 the same as parsed disagreement; the apparent consistency decline was the cap. 'Load degrades swap consistency' was withdrawn.
entries.repair: Score ungradeable responses as their own category; raise the cap and re-run (C1-D, 13b24a8).

entries.title: Treatment changed which units were gradeable
entries.defect: Conditioning accuracy on pairs that survived a swap-consistency filter made accuracy rise 0.857 to 0.930 (hypergeometric p=0.023 against random attrition) because the treatment changed which pairs survived.
entries.repair: Fixed denominator (all pairs) or a prespecified missingness model.

entries.title: Scoring convention selected among three that disagree
entries.defect: Three candidate scoring conventions gave three signs, one was in use, and the registered parse gate was never applied.
entries.repair: Register one convention; report the others as sensitivity only.

entries.title: Rebase destroyed priority proofs
entries.defect: Twelve seal hashes recorded in the ledger stopped existing after a rebase. The prose stayed accurate, the author even noted the rebase, and the proof of priority was gone.
entries.detected_by: pe_lint P1 on the converted corpus
entries.repair: Re-anchor: record the current commit beside the historical hash (s7.1.1); merge, never rebase, in a ledger repository.

entries.title: Disclosed post-seal amendment silently breaks the content hash
entries.defect: Amendments made after sealing were disclosed in the text, but they changed the registration body, so the recorded content hash no longer matched. Disclosure did not preserve the seal.
entries.gap: pe_lint verifies ancestry of the seal commit, not the registration's content hash.
entries.would_need: P1 sub-check: hash the registration blob at the seal commit and compare with the recorded hash; amendments live in a separate dated file (s3.2).

entries.title: Orphan correction: a thesis weakened with a blast radius of zero
entries.source: papers/tts/README.md (defect 2); papers/kuhn (Hart, primary rules without secondary)
entries.defect: 87 occurrences rewritten and 2,126 equations verified identical; the published book now reads as though the stronger claim was never made. No row records that a claim changed meaning.
entries.gap: No property ties a change in a claim's statement or scope to a version bump on its row. PE-CLS s10.4 leaves scope drift to humans.
entries.would_need: Claim semantic versioning (docs/kuhnian-path.md I-3): a statement or scope diff on a row with no major-version history entry is an error.

entries.title: Results graded above their own declared dependencies
entries.defect: Claims graded assumption-free while their dependency lists name modeling constructs.
entries.repair: Demote to the weakest load-bearing dependency, or promote the dependency on its own evidence.

entries.title: Priority does not propagate up a dependency (GO-12 on GO-11)
entries.defect: GO-12 is 'predicted' and rests on GO-11, which is 'replicated'. A prediction cannot inherit priority its support lacks; the edge was named in GO-12's own sealed prereg, so this is not a wiring artifact.
entries.detected_by: pe_lint P4 after the spine was wired
entries.repair: Owner decision on which class is wrong (acknowledged in baseline).

entries.title: L3 certified over an empty dependency graph
entries.defect: The validator certified L3 for a ledger with 0 of 78 claims carrying an edge, because the format had no edge field. Every P4 check passed over nothing.
entries.detected_by: reading the parser, not the report
entries.repair: Non-vacuity: report edge coverage, fail on an empty graph, cap edge-incapable formats at L2.

entries.title: Edges wired after the results, with no priority of their own
entries.defect: 27 edges were declared into a corpus whose results were all in, and the validator accepted every one: claims had a priority property and edges had none.
entries.repair: Edge provenance (declared / entered / declared_in); a backfill must name its sealed declaration.

entries.title: An undefined class token read as a live class
entries.defect: Two claims tagged '[refuted-as-sealed]', a token the spec does not define, were silently read as 'exploratory' (live) where the programme meant terminal.
entries.repair: Map the token to a defined class (the converter's CLASS_FIXUP does this for 'refuted-as-sealed'); the linter now refuses any undefined class on native objects. The markdown front end still cannot see an unmatched token.

entries.title: A table header counted as a claim
entries.defect: Every conformance report before the native conversion counted the ledger's header row as a claim.
entries.gap: Markdown front end is heuristic; native objects remove the failure but nothing checks a report's claim count against an independent count.
entries.would_need: Conformance reports state the parser's count and a second count from the source (e.g. registry rows), and fail on disagreement.

entries.title: Tests citing undeclared transformation families
entries.source: observation-theory-campaigns OD.toml; repaired d43edb7; PE-DSC-1.0 s3.2.1
entries.defect: Ten OD tests cited three families the registry never declared; generate.py then rendered 30 blank family slots in the published encyclopedia.
entries.repair: Backfill rows that say so: declared date from the sealed prereg, declared_in naming it, entered = the repair date.

entries.repair: declared_in names the sealed registration; deleting the offending tests is not an alternative repair.

entries.repair: State what was revised, or that nothing was and why (both were absorbed by the declaration: the bar gave way, not the claim).

entries.title: Retrospective claims classed 'predicted'
entries.source: geometric-observation native ledger: VI-10, VI-13, GO-EC-5, GO-EC-6, GO-EC-7 (pe_lint run 2026-10-17)
entries.defect: Claims whose rows name no sealed registration carry the class 'predicted'. Priority cannot be reconstructed after the data.
entries.repair: Reclass to the retrospective cap, or locate the sealed registration the converter missed.

entries.title: No design in the reference ledger was ever checked for admissibility
entries.defect: All 43 in-scope claims of the reference deployment carried no admissibility block.
entries.repair: Mark unassessed (no demotion, no further promotion) until A1-A4 are discharged.

entries.title: A result whose raw outputs were never committed
entries.defect: A 13.7-point degradation claim did not reproduce in five of six cells; the most probable cause was arm-label contamination during off-repo aggregation, and it could not be pinned because raw outputs were never committed.
entries.gap: PE-CLS s3.4 requires results committed, but pe_lint checks only that a result file exists at a seal-descendant commit, not that the aggregation's inputs are committed with it.
entries.would_need: A result manifest listing the raw files an aggregate was computed from, each hashed and committed; a missing input is an error.

entries.title: Withdrawn recorded as refuted (the near miss)
entries.defect: Recording DB-022 as 'refuted' would have manufactured a negative result from a broken instrument (n=40 re-measurement against n=200).
entries.gap: The withdrawn/refuted choice depends on whether the evidence was valid, which no record check can decide.
entries.would_need: Nothing mechanical; the class choice is a recorded human decision naming the rule (s4.2) and the evidence.

entries.title: A campaign record that stopped tracking its campaign
entries.defect: The accounting still reads 'gates drafted 1' and 'no self-test, probe or pilot has run' after C2, C3 and H1 were drafted, refused and self-tested.
entries.detected_by: verification of an outside draft's case study
entries.gap: No check compares a campaign's summary counts with the registrations actually present.
entries.would_need: Generated accounting: summary counts computed from the registration files, never typed.

entries.title: Prose asserting a status change the ledger never made
entries.defect: The draft says the audit 'changed the programme's claim states from testable or demonstrated to open'. The ledger says no claim was raised or lowered by a gate.
entries.detected_by: checking the draft against the record
entries.gap: P3 forbids it, but the reference implementation scans a fixed list of documents and parses registration ids, not claim-state assertions.
entries.would_need: P3 over every narrative file, with claim-state phrases resolved to ledger history.

entries.title: An outcome outside the vocabulary hides a failed test from D3
entries.source: found while building this benchmark, 2026-10-17 (fixture DB-019 written with outcome 'fail')
entries.defect: PE-DSC-1.0 s4 spells the outcome 'failed'. A test recorded as 'fail' is not in pe_lint's NEEDS_WITNESS set, so D3 skips it without a finding: the failed test needs no revision and no witness, and the registry reads clean.
entries.detected_by: a benchmark fixture that should have fired and did not
entries.repair: Spell the outcome as s4 does; the linter now refuses an outcome outside s4.

external.note: K-1 exit requires >= 20 entries not from the author's corpus. Candidate sources, none yet entered: published corrections and retractions with a stated mechanism, the RP:P / Many Labs development set once coded (RUBRIC-v0.md), and defect classes in Flake & Fried 2020 and Chester & Lasko 2021. Each must cite its source and be checked against it before entry.
